newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ACCC gives nod to Bunge's Defiance bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ACCC gives nod to Bunge's Defiance bid.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Wednesday it had no plans to intervene in Bunge Corp's proposed acquisition of flour miller and baker Defiance Mills Ltd.
Bunge Cereal Foods Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of the Brazil-based Bunge group, announced on Tuesday that it would offer A$1.70 per share for Queensland based Defiance.
The bid values the Australian company at about A$97 million.
The ACCC, Australia's competition watchdog, said Bunge approached the ACCC about two weeks ago to seek its view on the bid's relevance to the Trade Practices Act.

"The ACCC, drawing on its previous extensive knowledge of the flour milling and baking industries, concluded that the proposed acquisition was unlikely to lead to a substantial lessening of competition in either the flour or bread markets," the ACCC said.
"The main reason for this conclusion was that there is little overlap in the flour operations and no overlap in the baking operations of Bunge and Defiance," the ACCC said.
The ACCC said Bunge had told it that the takeover would have a pro-competitive effect as it would create a third force in milling and baking in Australia.

The ACCC said Bunge had said that if the takeover succeeded, it would have a better chance of competing with Goodman Fielder Ltd and George Weston Foods Ltd. "The ACCC considered these submissions to be persuasive," it said.
Defiance has not formally responded to the takeover offer but chairman Tom O'Brien has told Reuters the bid did not reflect the real value of the company.
Defiance shares were trading at A$1.80 on Wednesday afternoon, up 20 cents from Tuesday's close.
